_comment: Study and practice sources. Each entry says which sheet, which tab, how to
read it, and when the picked items are due. Override the whole file with the
STUDY_SOURCES_PATH env var, or a JSON list in STUDY_SOURCES.
backlog — a flat list of topics/questions/projects. Each sync picks the
next `daily_count` rows you have not been given yet.
weekly  — one row per week, keyed by a date column. Picks the row for the
current week and emits `item_columns` from it.
due_time is local (24h). Items land in the block of your day where that kind
of work actually happens, per your Daily-Schedule-Template.

items.title: evm.codes

items.title: The Move Book
items.note: The canonical reference. Abilities and the resource model are the interview.

items.title: Aptos docs
items.note: Same language, different object model. Knowing the contrast is the answer.

items.note: Your star — read the framework modules, not the node.

items.note: Your star — Move-specific bug classes, which are not the EVM's.

items.note: Your star — real cross-chain Move in production.

_comment: Themes are picked per day so no area quietly eats the week.
'daily' runs every day. One entry from 'cycle' runs alongside it,
advancing by date so the cycle is stable across restarts and you can
see what tomorrow holds. Tasks are filed proposed, like everything else.
'sources' names study_sources keys to run only on that theme's day.
remind=false means tracked and shown on /day but never a reminder.

daily.label: Web3 bounty
tasks: 6-10 Solodit findings — predict root cause and severity BEFORE reading — https://solodit.cyfrin.io/
One entry from smart-contract-vulnerabilities, explained from memory — https://github.com/kadenzipfel/smart-contract-vulnerabilities
